title: Sakana AI tests self-improvement through teams of one shared model
friendlyTitle: One AI model learns from a team of copies of itself
summary: Sakana AI and UC Berkeley’s MASS method has copies of one model solve tasks, judge results and revise their team workflow, then trains the shared model on selected executions. The researchers report better score per output token on several research benchmarks, while emphasizing that shared blind spots can make the model reward flawed work.
friendlySummary: Copies of the same model work together, choose their best results and use those examples for more training. The method improved some tests but can repeat mistakes that every copy misses.
whyItMatters: Self-improvement is only as trustworthy as its evaluator. Organizations experimenting with automated optimization should keep independent tests, external reviewers and stop conditions outside the model’s own improvement loop.
friendlyWhyItMatters: An AI should not be the only judge of its own progress. Independent checks are still needed.
